reader.requirement: Wherever GR6-GR19 speak of literal-1..5, an identifier-3..7 in that position supplies its whole content as the literal (trailing spaces included), read after GR3's treatment (edited and unsigned numeric as alphanumeric, signed numeric de-signed without a separate sign) and with its subscripts evaluated once first (GR5), whether it is a pattern, a BEFORE/AFTER delimiter, a replacement or a CONVERTING set.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel < 2002: at 85 the SR7/SR8/SR9 size rules ask identifier-3/5/6/7 static sizes at compile time; from 2002 only literals (identifier sizes become run-time EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE)

DialectBehavior.InspectBeforeFromFirstEligiblePosition (active from 2023): at 85 a BEFORE delimiter is searched from the leftmost position (beforeFromLeftmost=true), at 2023 from the AFTER-derived start

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior in InspectBinder#InspectCharOperandOf and InspectEmitter#OperandTextOf: none; the operand read is edition-invariant, and the listed sites gate the size syntax rules and where the BEFORE search starts
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the size rules (SR7/SR8/SR9) refuse a mis-sized identifier operand at compile time, from 2002 it is a run-time EC-RANGE-INSPECT-SIZE; the identifier-as-literal substitution itself is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf16_01 I1-I4 cover alphanumeric identifier-3/4/5/6/7 with trailing spaces; not exercised there: signed (overpunch and separate), unsigned and numeric-edited operands, subscripted operands, an AFTER identifier-4, the size refusals

probes.expected: the whole content, trailing space included

S9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -1 reads as 1; S9 -3 reads as 3; unsigned 9 and Z9 ' 4' as characters; identifier-4 as BEFORE and AFTER; identifiers 6/7; subscript TE (N2) evaluated before N2 is incremented (GR5)

probes.printed: COBOL0847 INSPECT operand 'G2' shall reference an elementary item
probes.expected: SR2: identifier-3 must be an elementary DISPLAY item

probes.printed: COBOL0846 identifier-6 and identifier-7 differ in size (§1985:VI.6.18.3 SR9)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR4  the text is in GR4 (quoted: "apply equally to the content of the data item referenced by identifier-3")
OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR3c  the text is in GR3c (quoted: "the original value of the sign is retained upon completion of the INSPECT statement")
OK  §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR5  the text is in GR5 (quoted: "evaluated only once as the first operation in the execution of the INSPECT statement")

reader.notes: Every operand position goes through InspectCharOperandOf to a BoundFieldOperand that OperandTextOf reads at run time (AsItemCharacters, deSign: true), so the identifier stands for the literal in every rule. Subscripts are frozen in IdentifyOperands before any counter is stored.

refuter.evidence: q1.cob (q1-002, --std 85): a signed identifier-5 S9 -3 as the replacement gave I1=[33X3]. A signed identifier-7 S99 -12 gave I2=[1212]. A signed identifier-4 gave I3=02 as BEFORE and I6=[AA3zz ] as AFTER in format 4. A numeric-edited identifier-3 PIC -9 "-3" is read with its edit character: I4=02. An identifier-6 with SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE reads de-signed: I5=[abab--]. q2.cob: 1985 Amendment 1 admits an alphanumeric function-identifier wherever a sending identifier is permitted, and one stands correctly for literal-1 (F1=02), literal-3 (F2=[babaXA]), literal-4 and literal-5 (F3=[cbacba]) and literal-2 (F4=03). Refusals: rf a COMP identifier-3 COBOL0847 (SR2); rd and re, 2002 literal classes, COBOL0900. Side observation outside this rule: CONVERTING SS2 TO "ab", with SS2 PIC S99 SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE, is refused with COBOL0846 because SR9 compares the item's 3-character size. That is SR9's reading of size, not GR4. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR4 ("apply equally to the content of the data item referenced by identifier-3"); OK §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR3c; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR3 ("may be specified anywhere in the general formats that an identifier is permitted").
